subject: EU/APAC standby verification and evidence readout
messages:
From: Simon Hansen <simon.hansen@nordichealth.dk>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-16T09:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Private deployment – residency & failover evidence request

Hi Logan,

Thanks for the earlier walkthrough. Our security team wants a concise package showing how Redwood Private would behave for a primary EU site with a warm-standby in APAC. Specifically:

- Proof that data from EU-resident customers remains within EU under normal ops.
- What exact conditions cause traffic/state to cross to APAC (latency thresholds, capacity thresholds, control-plane failover).
- A short checklist we can hand to our auditors for a live failover test and acceptance criteria.

Can you send a readout and any supporting artifacts (network diagrams, checklist, who owns cutover authorization)? We are aiming for an internal audit the week of Apr 30.

Regards,
Simon Hansen
Head of Cloud Security – Nordic Health
[simon.hansen@nordichealth.dk]

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Simon Hansen <simon.hansen@nordichealth.dk>

Date: 2028-04-16T10:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Private deployment – residency & failover evidence request

Hi Simon — thanks for the clear list.

Quick summary: we can provide a tight evidence bundle (network map, control-plane decision log, and a five-step verification checklist) and run a short, recorded failover exercise during the audit window. Two notes up front:

1) There are two failure modes that can drive APAC handling: a) customer-configured regional routing (explicit policy), and b) automated fallback when the EU dedicated pool drops below a configured capacity SLO (we treat this as a controlled escalation). We will document thresholds for both.
2) The control-plane remains in your VPC for Private deployments; key sync and handoff logs are retained in-region by default, we’ll include retention proofs.

Ill put the internal readout together and propose a verification script. Would Apr 30 at 09:00 CET work for a 45-minute session?

Attachments: standby-verification-checklist.xlsx (draft), apac-eu-network-map.v1.pdf

Best,
Logan Wright
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.com

Team — copying the thread in case you didn’t see Simon’s ask. Key deliverables:

- One-page evidence pack that demonstrates in-region data custody + control-plane decision trail.

Lauren: can you take the evidence pack (include retention proof and KMS/HSM pointers)?
Marcus: need a concise note on how routing policies vs capacity fallback are triggered — include exact config fields and thresholds we recommend.
Soojin: coordinate a short recording of the failover exercise (we’ll run in your staging VPC and mirror steps for the customer).

I attached a draft checklist. Ive penciled Apr 30 09:00 CET for the external demo/readout. Please reply with blockers by EOD Apr 18.

— Logan

Got it. Ill own the evidence pack. Items Im adding to the checklist:

- Audit log excerpt showing control-plane authorization for a previous internal cutover (redacted).
- KMS key policy snapshot for EU keys + HSM attestation reference.
- Retention statement and sample query proving no cross-region replication for customer data by default.

Questions for the group:
- Marcus, do we have a hard limit on how long we keep KV cache entries when failing over? Customers will want to know how tokenization and session state behave.
- Logan, for the scheduled run we should capture both application-level correctness (routing to a read replica) and proof of custody logs.

I will circulate the evidence pack draft by Apr 18 EOD.

Thanks —
Lauren Bishop
Head of Product Ops, Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, soojin.lee@redwood.com, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-18T13:14:00Z
Subject: Re: INTERNAL: Prep for Nordic Health readout (Apr 30)

Short answers:

- KV cache TTLs: default is 24h for session artifacts; during a controlled warm-standby switchover we flush session KV caches for the affected customer namespace unless the customer opts into sticky-cache replication (weve made this opt-in because of PII concerns). Ill add the exact config keys and an example rollout snippet to the checklist.
- Routing thresholds: automated failover kicks when EU dispatch success rate falls below 85% for 3 consecutive minutes AND the cluster-level health score drops below 0.7. We can make those thresholds configurable at deployment time — add that to the acceptance criteria.

I attached a short network map overlay (apac-eu-network-map.v1.pdf) and a sample config snippet.

Marcus Lin
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

- Draft evidence pack attached (standby-verification-checklist.xlsx): one-page summary + acceptance criteria, sample audit log snippets, and a minimal playbook for a warm-standby exercise.
- We propose to run the live verification on Apr 30 09:00 CET. Runbook will be executed in your staging VPC (CloudPort will help with peering).
